headline: Terence Tao argues that mathematics must stop treating problem-solving as its main goal now that AI can produce proofs in bulk.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: read in full and new today, but it is one mathematician's argument reported by a single outlet.
importance_line: Mathematicians, students and journals get a leading voice arguing that the flood of AI-solved problems should change what the field rewards and teaches, but it is one mathematician's view, as described by a single outlet.
summary: OfficeChai reports that Fields Medalist Terence Tao has published "Math 2.0", an October 2026 slide deck arguing that AI has made proofs plentiful, so mathematics must now decide what it is for rather than treat solving open problems as the goal. It follows the call to stop working with OpenAI that Tao shared from a mathematicians' group, which our 9 Oct 2026 edition carried from The Decoder after OpenAI released hundreds of AI-written maths manuscripts at once; the deck itself warns that checking an AI's answer is not enough unless a human also understands why it works.
notes: Follow-up of the 10 Oct 2026 entry (36Kr: Tao reposted the group's call) and the 9 Oct 2026 entry (The Decoder). Single outlet; the deck was not opened. Outlets differ on the group's name and the number of proofs (see facts file), so neither is stated as fact here.
